claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me first review the official eligibility criteria to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. Now I can help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 19 and not in approved education or training, I need to understand his situation a bit better.

When did Alex finish his education or training? (Or if he never completed any, when did he leave school?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a while back, maybe around six months ago or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Does Alex currently live with you in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me. He's living elsewhere at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask:

Are you currently contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep? This could include paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing to his accommodation costs.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes and helping with his living costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to know:

How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep? And is this on a regular basis (for example, weekly or monthly)?

(For reference, the current Child Benefit rate for an only or eldest child is £25.60 per week, which is approximately £110.93 per month)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I give him £30 a week, regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not working that much - just does a bit here and there, nothing like a full-time job. And no, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit for children under 16 is available if you're responsible for them. However, for young people aged 16-19 (which includes Alex at 19), they must be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit.

Since Alex left school about 6 months ago and is not currently in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit, even though you are contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep.

The contribution rules that allow Child Benefit to continue when a child lives elsewhere only apply to children who still meet the basic eligibility requirements - such as being under 16, or being 16-19 and in approved education or training.

If Alex were to return to approved education or training in the future, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again at that point, provided he remains under 20 years old.

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old and is not in approved education or training. According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16-19 only if they stay in approved education or training. Alex left school approximately 6 months ago and is not currently in any approved education or training. While the claimant is contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an only/eldest child), and Alex does not live with the claimant, this does not change the fundamental eligibility requirement. The contribution rule applies when a child 'goes to live with someone else' - allowing Child Benefit to continue beyond the initial 8 weeks if contributions are made. However, this provision applies to children who still meet the basic age and education criteria. Since Alex is over 16 and not in approved education or training, he does not meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit, regardless of the contributions being made. Alex is also not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right, but this does not restore eligibility - it's simply that he doesn't meet the positive criteria for continuing Child Benefit beyond age 16.
